methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
VEIR, a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Tim Heidel, has raised $117M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the climate and energy sector, including peers at Series C stage such as KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, which applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $222M based on the $117M raised proxy. Peer-median analysis across the three referenced Series C comparables produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with the peer set ranging from $700M to $3.0B. The stage-progression approach anchors to VEIR's current funding to date, while the peer-median method reflects valuations of more mature but functionally comparable businesses in the same sector.

Triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $189M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $611M. The wide dispersion—driven primarily by the difference between stage-adjusted fundraising and peer-comparable multiples—reflects material uncertainty about VEIR's relative progress versus the peer set. Key sensitivities include the comparability of peer revenue profiles and near-term capital efficiency relative to existing Series C-stage companies in the climate technology space.
